title: SMB Quickstart Pack — Pricing & Onramp Playbook
author: Priya Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines the 'SMB Quickstart Pack' — a compact product offering and onboarding path tailored to small and early-stage customers who need fast time-to-value, predictable costs, and low operational overhead. The document covers the product overview, minimum viable requirements (PRD), integration design constraints, a staged roadmap for launch, pricing and packaging details, release notes checklist for field teams, and runbook-style onboarding flow.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-integration to < 3 days for typical developer workflows.
- Offer a clear consumption-to-cost mapping with predictable monthly pricing and optional usage tiers.
- Provide out-of-the-box guards that preserve platform SLOs: 99.5% request success, p95 latency < 250ms for token generation under typical usage profiles.
- Enable self-serve upgrade path to Dedicated/Private offerings.

Target customers and personas:
- Product and engineering teams at SMBs and startups with 1–10 engineers.
- Primary personas: CTO/Founding engineer (purchase decision), Lead engineer (integration), Product manager (prioritization).

Quickstart pack components (what is included):
1) Developer toolkit (self-serve):
   - SDK starter repo (Node, Python) with sample prompts and a small demo app.
   - Preconfigured telemetry dashboard template in Redwood Console (token-cost, per-route latency, errors).
2) Cost & SLO presets:
   - Default batching and cache profiles tuned for low-burst SMB workloads.
   - Safety caps (per-tenant token per-minute limits) and automated throttling policies.
3) Prebaked prompts and evals:
   - 3 starter prompt-sets for common use cases (summarization, support triage, code assist) and lightweight eval harness.
4) Onboarding credits and migration path:
   - 30-day trial with $300 usage credit and 10k free embedding units.
   - Direct upgrade link to Dedicated with migration checklist.

MVP requirements (product requirement checklist):
- PRD-001: Self-serve sign-up flow that provisions a tenant with default Quickstart policy.
- PRD-002: One-click SDK scaffold (Python/Node) containing sample app that authenticates and calls Redwood API.
- PRD-003: Console experience: prebuilt dashboard template and cost alert pre-configured (alert at 70% credit consumption).
- PRD-004: Cost caps and throttles: per-tenant rate limit at 2 requests/s and 10k tokens/min by default.
- PRD-005: Telemetry tags: route, model_variant, tenant_id must be present in telemetry for all Quickstart tenants.
- PRD-006: Billing integration: usage tagging to map Quickstart SKU for credit consumption.

Acceptance criteria (how we will know it’s done):
- 90% of test customers complete the sample integration (token exchange + first generation) within 3 days.
- No Quickstart tenant causes average p95 latency degradation > 5% across hosted pool over a 7-day window.
- Billing reconciliation reports Quickstart usage correctly for 100% of test transactions.

Design constraints and engineering notes:
- Service boundary: Quickstart will run entirely on Hosted (no Dedicated routing by default).
- Runtime profile: Small batch sizes (max_batch_size=8), KV cache warmup disabled initially to keep memory profile predictable.
- Telemetry hooks: Metrics emitted to 'quickstart' telemetry namespace. Required tags: tenant_id, route, model, variant, billing_sku.
- Security: Default tenant role: "developer-quickstart" with scoped API key and no access to private deployment features.
- Fallback policy: Requests that exceed soft limits will receive HTTP 429 with 'x-retry-after' header; after 3 consecutive 429s, route is flagged for opt-in support outreach.

Sample configuration snippet (to be included in SDK starter README):

# Quickstart client config (YAML)
api_key: "<REDACTED>"
model: "redwood-compact-1"
max_tokens: 512
batch_profile: "quickstart-small"
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  namespace: "quickstart"

(Team: Developer Experience will include this file in starter repos.)

Roadmap & launch milestones (quarterly view):
- Q3 2026 (MVP): Self-serve flows, SDK scaffold, console dashboard, billing tagging, trial credits.
- Q4 2026: Add templated prompt library, lightweight eval harness, upgrade path to Dedicated.
- Q1 2027: Add localized docs (EU, APAC), automated migration assistant for Dedicated customers, and partner reseller packaging.

Pricing & packaging (recommended tiers):
- Quickstart Basic (monthly): $49/mo 
  - Includes: 30k tokens/month included, developer SDK, console template, community support.
  - Overages: $0.0008 per token after included quota.
- Quickstart Pro (monthly): $249/mo
  - Includes: 300k tokens/month, 10k embedding units, email support, 24-hour ticket SLA.
  - Overages: $0.0006 per token; preemptible warm capacity option +10% on request.
- Quickstart Growth (monthly commitment): $999/mo (discounted annual)
  - Includes: 1.5M tokens/month, 100k embedding units, onboarding call, dedicated success manager (shared).
  - Overages: $0.00045 per token; migration credit to Dedicated (up to $2k) on annual upgrade.

Packaging rules & constraints:
- All Quickstart plans include the 30-day trial offer once per account.
- Migration credit is additive and must be applied within 90 days of upgrading to Dedicated.
- Any pro-rated refunds follow standard billing policy; exceptions require finance approval.

Release notes (for product & sales):
- v1.0 (2026-09-10): Launch Quickstart Basic & Pro tiers, SDK starter repos published, console dashboard template available, trial credit code generation enabled.
- Known limitations: No Dedicated routing from Quickstart by default; KV cache disabled for memory predictability; EU data residency compliance not available in MVP.

Customer onboarding play (step-by-step):
1) Customer signs up and receives Quickstart tenant and trial credits.
2) Customer follows Quickstart README and runs sample app (CLI: `npm run quickstart` or `python -m quickstart`).
3) Once sample succeeds, encourage team to import one prompt set and enable console dashboard.
4) At 70% credit consumption, automated email with recommended SKU upgrade is sent.
5) If scaling above 1M tokens/month, present Dedicated migration checklist and offer migration credit.

Runbook: Operational escalation (SRE + Product)
- If tenant causes sustained p95 latency > 250ms for 10 minutes: automatically reduce batch concurrency and notify owner.
- If billing tag failures exceed 0.1% of events in 24h: block new Quickstart signups and page Billing on-call.
- If trial credit consumption spikes > 5x expected: throttle and create a support ticket; send product-team alert to examine prompts/abuse.

Ownership and contacts (who does what):
- Product (owner): Priya Patel — product strategy, roadmap, pricing.
- DevEx (owner): Diego Morales — SDKs, starter repos, README, onboarding flows.
- Console (owner): Anika Rao — dashboard templates, alerts.
- Billing & Finance: Liam O'Connor — pricing rules, credits, reconciliation.
- SRE: On-call rotation (see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks for paging).

Risk, mitigations and open questions:
- Risk: Quickstart tenants may attract high-cost generative workloads and impact pool economics.
  - Mitigation: conservative default caps, automated throttles, early telemetry tagging for cost signals.
- Risk: Confusion between Quickstart and Dedicated feature sets.
  - Mitigation: In-console banners and an explicit 'Upgrade to Dedicated' UX with migration checklist.
- Open question: Do we allow limited KV cache for Pro tier? (Action: Prod + Runtime teams to triage and provide memory profile estimates by 2026-10-01.)

Appendix: Sample outreach template for sales/CS after 70% credit consumption:

Subject: Quickstart usage: recommend next steps
Hi <Customer>,

We’re seeing strong usage of your Quickstart pack — you’re at 72% of trial credits. If you’d like predictable costs and higher throughput, we recommend Quickstart Pro or beginning a Dedicated evaluation. I’m happy to schedule a 30-minute session to review usage patterns and migration options.

Best,
<Success Manager>
